Sentence (English): This LG dishwasher is very spacious, the convenience with which the different components of the dishes are loaded is appreciated, it has a capacity for 14 place settings and you do not have problems with the height of the plates, since you have the option of varying the height of the trays in a very simple way.
Comments (English): [ Muy satisfecho ] || ---------------- || This LG dishwasher is very spacious, the convenience with which the different components of the dishes are loaded is appreciated, it has a capacity for 14 place settings and you do not have problems with the height of the plates, since you have the option of varying the height of the trays in a very simple way. Even the 3 cutlery tray has a part that we can adjust to place small cups. As for the washing cycles, there are all kinds and specific depending on the type of dishes we want to wash, Auto, turbo, intensive. We even have the option of downloading some more from the app, one special for pots and pans, another for glassware, one called night care, special for washing silently during the night. We can choose half load, it also allows us to indicate if we have placed it on the upper or lower tray or choose a softer spray level for the upper tray and more powerful for the lower one, so we can place very dirty pots on the lower one and the dishes normal at the top. Another option to highlight is the connectivity with the LGThinQ app, in addition to allowing us to download more washing cycles as I have already mentioned, it allows us to keep track of the state of the dishwasher, notifies us when we must clean the appliance (every 30 cycles ) and notifies us with a notification when the wash cycle has finished. Finally, I really liked the result of the different cycles that I have tried, it hardly makes any noise and the dishes have come out perfect, thanks to cleaning with steam it comes out without a single water mark, the purchase has been all a success.
Comments (Original): [ Muy satisfecho ] || ---------------- || Este lavavajillas LG es muy espacioso, se agradece la comodidad con que se cargan los diferentes componentes de la vajilla, tiene capacidad para 14 cubiertos y no tienes problemas con la altura de los platós, ya que tienes la opción de variar la altura de las bandejas de una forma muy simple. Incluso la 3 bandeja para cubiertos tiene una parte que podemos ajustar para colocar tazas pequeñas. En cuanto a los ciclos de lavado hay de todo tipo y específicos según el tipo de vajilla que queremos lavar, Auto, turbo, intensivo... Incluso tenemos la opción de descargar algunos más desde la app, uno especial para ollas y sartenes, otro para cristalerías, uno denominado cuidado nocturno, especial para lavar de forma silenciosa durante la noche. Podemos elegir media carga, además nos permite indicar si la hemos colocado en la bandeja superior o inferior o elegir un nivel de pulverización más suave para la bandeja superior y más potente para la inferior, así podemos colocar ollas muy sucias en la inferior y la vajilla normal en la superior. Otra opción a destacar es la conectividad con la app LGThinQ, además de permitirnos descargar más ciclos de lavado como ya he comentado anteriormente, nos permite llevar un seguimiento del estado del lavavajillas, nos avisa de cuando debemos hacer una limpieza del aparato (cada 30 ciclos) y nos avisa con una notificación de cuando ha terminado el ciclo de lavado. Por último, el resultado de los diferentes ciclos que he probado me ha gustado mucho, no hace apenas nada de ruido y la vajilla ha salido perfecta, gracias a la limpieza con vapor de agua sale sin una sola marca de agua, la compra ha sido todo un acierto.

Sentence (English): So we found this dishwasher to replace another GE dishwasher- the price point was right for us.
Comments (English): [ It gets better… give it a while to grow on you ] || ---------------- || So we found this dishwasher to replace another GE dishwasher- the price point was right for us. We would have rather had a stainless interior but we had to make a couple concessions here and there. With the promo, we felt like we'd chosen a pretty nice dishwasher for the price- it had some features that are old when did not. It has a digital display which is nice because you can see how much time is left and things like that. We like that the handle is on the front so we can hang a dish towel on it. Sentence (English): This is by far the best cleaning dishwasher I've seen.
Comments (English): [ Cleans well, but loading is challenging ] || ---------------- || This is by far the best cleaning dishwasher I've seen. Eveything comes out spotless and without issues. Using it is easy and intuitive, and I use the recommended product from Finish to clean with. The issues come when trying to load the racks. Top rack is good for silverware, flat serving spoons, spatuals etc. Small covers get put there as well. On the second rack, half is very usefull for loading small bowls and glasses. There is half of the rack with narrow spaced tines that accept the smaller bowls, but bigger bowls just fall over and take up too much room. The other half has very widely spaced tines that accept glasses and larger bowl, but will not keep anything from falling over. I'm not sure what the mini shelves that fold out from the right side are used for so I took them out. I would never stack anything on them as they would probably become projectiles during the wash cycle. The lowest rack is worthless for anything that is not a very flat plate. The tines are not well spaced out to accept any kind of bowl. Thin dishes will fit ok, but anything with a deeper mold to it will not fit. If you put your pots and pans in it, they will take up most of the room cause there are tines spaced for that type of cookware. All in all the tines are too close and too short to hold anything properly. The bottom rack usually is where the biggest stuff will go but the rack is just shaped poorly for our dishes and bowls. We get by with running it more often when we can space out everything, but if you have a large load of dishs and cookware it will be challenging to get it all loaded.

Comments (English): [ Muy satisfecho ] || ---------------- || This LG dishwasher is very spacious, the convenience with which the different components of the dishes are loaded is appreciated, it has a capacity for 14 place settings and you do not have problems with the height of the plates, since you have the option of varying the height of the trays in a very simple way. Even the 3 cutlery tray has a part that we can adjust to place small cups. As for the washing cycles, there are all kinds and specific depending on the type of dishes we want to wash, Auto, turbo, intensive. We even have the option of downloading some more from the app, one special for pots and pans, another for glassware, one called night care, special for washing silently during the night. We can choose half load, it also allows us to indicate if we have placed it on the upper or lower tray or choose a softer spray level for the upper tray and more powerful for the lower one, so we can place very dirty pots on the lower one and the dishes normal at the top. Another option to highlight is the connectivity with the LGThinQ app, in addition to allowing us to download more washing cycles as I have already mentioned, it allows us to keep track of the state of the dishwasher, notifies us when we should clean the appliance (every 30 cycles ) and notifies us with a notification when the wash cycle has finished. Finally, I really liked the result of the different cycles that I have tried, it hardly makes any noise and the dishes have come out perfect, thanks to cleaning with steam it comes out without a single water mark, the purchase has been all a success.
Comments (Original): [ Muy satisfecho ] || ---------------- || Este lavavajillas LG es muy espacioso, se agradece la comodidad con que se cargan los diferentes componentes de la vajilla, tiene capacidad para 14 cubiertos y no tienes problemas con la altura de los platós, ya que tienes la opción de variar la altura de las bandejas de una forma muy simple. Incluso la 3 bandeja para cubiertos tiene una parte que podemos ajustar para colocar tazas pequeñas. En cuanto a los ciclos de lavado hay de todo tipo y específicos según el tipo de vajilla que queremos lavar, Auto, turbo, intensivo... Incluso tenemos la opción de descargar algunos más desde la app, uno especial para ollas y sartenes, otro para cristalerías, uno denominado cuidado nocturno, especial para lavar de forma silenciosa durante la noche. Podemos elegir media carga, además nos permite indicar si la hemos colocado en la bandeja superior o inferior o elegir un nivel de pulverización más suave para la bandeja superior y más potente para la inferior, así podemos colocar ollas muy sucias en la inferior y la vajilla normal en la superior. Otra opción a destacar es la conectividad con la app LGThinQ, además de permitirnos descargar más ciclos de lavado como ya he comentado anteriormente, nos permite llevar un seguimiento del estado del lavavajillas, nos avisa de cuando debemos hacer una limpieza del aparato (cada 30 ciclos) y nos avisa con una notificación de cuando ha terminado el ciclo de lavado. Por último, el resultado de los diferentes ciclos que he probado me ha gustado mucho, no hace apenas nada de ruido y la vajilla ha salido perfecta, gracias a la limpieza con vapor de agua sale sin una sola marca de agua, la compra ha sido todo un acierto.

Sentence (English): This is the second Bosch dishwasher I have owned.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, sleek, efficient ] || ---------------- || This is the second Bosch dishwasher I have owned. The first one stayed in the house when I sold it. I really like the cutlery tray, and use this for some of my small shallow containers as well. The top rack for cups and glasses has 3 adjustable levels and is easy to adjust. For ease, I wash wine glasses on the bottom rack. We have 29 cm dinner plates which just fit in, if the upper rack is on its highest setting. It is easy to operate and cleans the dishes really well. I like the extra dry option as well. We were undecided if we wanted the buttons hidden on the inner top or not, but they are easy to use and no risk of kids or people leaning on them and starting the dishwasher! The down side is that you cant see how much longer there is left for the dishwasher to finish. The underbench installation instructions were pictures, and the QR codes were computer generated images, so it took us a while to work out how to install it. It would be much better if there were some QR codes to some handy hints and also to a video with a human talking and showing an installation.

Sentence (English): I give this dishwasher an average review based on the cost, design and function compared to our previous KitchenAid dishwasher of 12 years.
Comments (English): [ Samsung Bespoke Linear Wash Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I give this dishwasher an average review based on the cost, design and function compared to our previous KitchenAid dishwasher of 12 years. The Samsung dishwasher cost more than the equivalent of a new KitchenAid and is substandard with the following: There are many fewer stems on each rack, allowing for fewer dishes to be loaded overall; the racks are very flimsy in design when pulling open and pushing to close; the stainless steel front is a cheap plastic coated to look like stainless steel; the type of linear dishwashing method leaves much more water in lips of coffee mugs, plastic wear, etc., despite using JetDry and utilizing the auto door opening once a cycle has finished in order to release steam and continue drying the dishes. My dish towel is soaked after drying dishes with all the remaining water. On the positive, the dishes have been completely clean and dry (other than previously indicated). It seems to function and clean very well on any cycle and is extremely quiet. We have had a Samsung Bespoke refrigerator for 6 months and a Samsung stove for 5 years and have been happy with them, however it appears that Samsung is getting cheaper in their quality, yet remaining rather high priced. Wish I had stayed with KitchenAid or other tried and true higher end brand for dishwasher. I will rethink Samsung brand for future purchases.

The Samsung dishwasher cost more than the equivalent of a new KitchenAid and is substandard with the following: There are many fewer stems on each rack, allowing for fewer dishes to be loaded overall; the racks are very flimsy in design when pulling open and pushing to close; the stainless steel front is a cheap plastic coated to look like stainless steel; the type of linear dishwashing method leaves much more water in lips of coffee mugs, plastic wear, etc., despite using JetDry and utilizing the auto door opening once a cycle has finished in order to release steam and continue drying the dishes. My dish towel is soaked after drying dishes with all the remaining water. On the positive, the dishes have been completely clean and dry (other than previously indicated). It seems to function and clean very well on any cycle and is extremely quiet. We have had a Samsung Bespoke refrigerator for 6 months and a Samsung stove for 5 years and have been happy with them, however it appears that Samsung is getting cheaper in their quality, yet remaining rather high priced. Wish I had stayed with KitchenAid or other tried and true higher end brand for dishwasher. I will rethink Samsung brand for future purchases.

Sentence (English): I've had this dishwasher less than 3 years after buying it new.
Comments (English): [ Lots of Trouble ] || ---------------- || I've had this dishwasher less than 3 years after buying it new. It does a good job cleaning the dishes and is relatively quiet. I like the bottle jets and it has a pretty good layout.Within 6 months it was sporadically leaking and we requested a repair under warranty. The repairman couldn't find the leak during his visit so he made some adjustments. About 6 months later it dumped water on the floor. A little rubber elbow had failed, and because each end is a different diameter I couldn't find a replacement without ordering a new sump pump.Less than a year after replacing the sump pump the washer started to leak again. This time it was from the plugs on the heater connections which had come loose and the rubber gaskets were failing to seal.Additionally the chrome trim around the control console on the door keeps popping out and the silverware rack eroded away until the bottom broke out.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is not worth $1,349 AT ALL!
Comments (English): This dishwasher is not worth $1,349 AT ALL! The only good thing about it is how quiet it is which wasn't even a feature I needed. The racks are so poorly designed it maybe holds half the dishes my old one did. The slanted prongs are too close to the edges so I can't fit dishes or larger items in there. They also are too close together so my plates barely fit and certain baby/toddler plates are too wide for them. Also, the slanted prongs change directions in half of the rack so items going one way take up space so I can't place items going the other way. (See pic). It's also supposed to have this superior drying which is one of the things I paid extra for and dishes are not dry. The sprayers sometimes flip over Tupperware containers so then they are right side up and full of water when the cycle is done. I tried posting a video of how my dishes do not fit in the prongs all the way, but it will not allow me to upload it. I could have saved hundreds of dollars on a different dishwasher.

Sentence (English): I bought this in January (my first KitchenAid appliance), and it was delivered and installed in February.
Comments (English): [ Has never worked properly, fixing takes months ] || ---------------- || I bought this in January (my first KitchenAid appliance), and it was delivered and installed in February. After a few days of seeming to work normally, I woke up to an alarm on the dishwasher in the middle of the night, and it had not drained. I called to have it fixed with the warranty, and until the repair person came, I was able to get the dishwasher to limp along by pushing the "drain" button after the cycle, and then running a rinse cycle to wash the residue off the dishes, and having to push "drain" again after that. At one point, it stopped draining entirely and I had to use a shop vac to get the water out. After a few weeks, the repair person game, said it was the drain pump, and ordered a replacement (he didn't have it in stock). A few weeks later, he returned, and replaced the pump, but the dishwasher still had the same problem. He ordered a replacement control panel and had to wait several weeks for that to arrive. In the meantime, the dishwasher wouldn't even finish a cycle (even without draining), so my wife and I have been hand washing dishes for about a month. with a newborn baby in the house. It is now the month of May, and I'm waiting for the service appointment to supposedly fix it once and for all. It's been almost three months since the dishwasher was installed, and except for the first few days, it has never worked properly. I called KitchenAid customer service, and they said they will not replace it until three different service visits have happened, and the technician determines that it is not fixable. I am extremely dissatisfied with the product and the warranty service (they don't have any parts in stock, and therefore have to order them AFTER visiting to determine what's wrong, taking more time away from my job to meet the tech, and then the parts are back ordered and take weeks to arrive). I can't imagine if I had this problem with my refrigerator and had to keep my groceries on ice in coolers for THREE MONTHS. I had planned to replace all my kitchen appliances with KitchenAid products so that they all matched (this was the first appliance purchased toward that goal), but after this experience, I don't plan to purchase any more KitchenAid appliances because they are not reliable and can't be quickly repaired. I thought I was purchasing a high quality product (the price certainly was very high), and instead, I wish I had my old dishwasher back because even if it was loud. it WORKED. Shame on you KitchenAid.

After a few days of seeming to work normally, I woke up to an alarm on the dishwasher in the middle of the night, and it had not drained. I called to have it fixed with the warranty, and until the repair person came, I was able to get the dishwasher to limp along by pushing the "drain" button after the cycle, and then running a rinse cycle to wash the residue off the dishes, and having to push "drain" again after that. At one point, it stopped draining entirely and I had to use a shop vac to get the water out. After a few weeks, the repair person game, said it was the drain pump, and ordered a replacement (he didn't have it in stock). A few weeks later, he returned, and replaced the pump, but the dishwasher still had the same problem. He ordered a replacement control panel and had to wait several weeks for that to arrive. In the meantime, the dishwasher wouldn't even finish a cycle (even without draining), so my wife and I have been hand washing dishes for about a month. with a newborn baby in the house. It is now the month of May, and I'm waiting for the service appointment to supposedly fix it once and for all. It's been almost three months since the dishwasher was installed, and except for the first few days, it has never worked properly. I called KitchenAid customer service, and they said they will not replace it until three different service visits have happened, and the technician determines that it is not fixable. I am extremely dissatisfied with the product and the warranty service (they don't have any parts in stock, and therefore have to order them AFTER visiting to determine what's wrong, taking more time away from my job to meet the tech, and then the parts are back ordered and take weeks to arrive). I can't imagine if I had this problem with my refrigerator and had to keep my groceries on ice in coolers for THREE MONTHS. I had planned to replace all my kitchen appliances with KitchenAid products so that they all matched (this was the first appliance purchased toward that goal), but after this experience, I don't plan to purchase any more KitchenAid appliances because they are not reliable and can't be quickly repaired. I thought I was purchasing a high quality product (the price certainly was very high), and instead, I wish I had my old dishwasher back because even if it was loud. it WORKED. Shame on you KitchenAid.

We like the timer on the front of the unit that allows you to see how long a selected wash/dry combo will take and then counts down as the unit runs. We chose a model with front controls given issues we have had with the keypads on top control units. Racks are sturdy and slide easily. Unit snaps shut for a tight seal. Stainless steel tub was a must have criteria for us as stainless steel seems to be easier to keep clean and helps with heat retention. We have noticed that his unit is a bit louder than others – but still quiet compared to units of years ago. Overall, very pleased with the unit so far.

Sentence (English): I have had this dishwasher for a week and have used it twice.
Comments (English): [ Almost Perfect ] || ---------------- || I have had this dishwasher for a week and have used it twice. I have been without a functioning dishwasher for about 20 years. I woke up last week and said I'm getting a brand new dishwasher. I selected this one and was so excited to finally have a dishwasher. I wish the pamphlet would have been more detailed on how to operate the different functions. I found the dishwasher to be quiet. Anything compared to this extremely loud Whirlpool refrigerator I have is a blessing. The dishes come out spotless and I am thankful for that. Now on the con side, my only issue is that the dishes don't throughly dry. I will say 80% do but not all. My first time I had everything set to normal. Last night I selected boost because of the instructions. As you can see from the pictures there is still alot of wetness on the door and inside. Because I have been without a dishwasher for so long, I am just happy the dishes are clean. With that said, this is not a deal breaker but if the unit dried throughly I could have given this review 5 stars. I know I read in the reviews when deciding to purchase, another lady had the same issue. I was looking for the dealers response to her in case I was doing something wrong. I can no longer find the comment. If the dealer is still reading comments, please tell me how to get all the dishes fully dried.

Sentence (English): Do yourself a favor- Don't buy a KitchenAid dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Run Away from KitchenAid Dishwashers ] || ---------------- || Do yourself a favor- Don't buy a KitchenAid dishwasher. I purchased one in a hurry and one month or less out of warranty the water wouldn't evacuate and the dishes weren't getting clean. I recommend Bosh Dishwashers- had one for many years at another house with no problems.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher a month ago, and it has been a major disappointment.
Comments (English): [ Much louder than advertised ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher a month ago, and it has been a major disappointment. It's supposed to be 44 dB but I measure it at 58 to 60 dB. It makes a grinding noise about every 1 to 2 seconds during the wash and rinse cycles that can be heard from the next room. The insulation under the door also keeps dropping down into view. During the first week, I contacted the installer to see if the noise problem was due to the insulation problem. When he came out, he simply stuffed the insulation back up in there (it still falls down) and told me the noise level is what I should expect. I then contacted KitchenAid about the issue, and they sent someone to check it out. First, he took the insulation that was falling down and stuffed it behind the floor face plate (not where it's supposed to go). Then he did diagnostics on the unit and found nothing wrong. He said the sound I am hearing is normal. He claimed that the 44 dB rating applies only to the motor itself. He thinks the sound I'm hearing is the water splashing against the walls of the steel tub. He suggested I try to reposition the dirty dishes to block the side walls. I told him that the dishwasher makes the same sound whether it's half-full or completely full. Then he said that the holes in the spray arms are much smaller now than they used to be, which causes less water to shoot out. That sounds like it contradicts his explanation. The sound I hear seems to be coming from the pump every time the water spurts into the spray arms. I now use the time-delay feature, so the dishwasher starts after we are in bed. I am debating on asking for an exchange to the 39 dB model. I am attaching a video so you can hear the noise level. Turn the volume up and then you can decide for yourself if you want to live with this noise level before you buy. The two good things about this model are the Pro-Dry fan feature, and the expanded capacity to hold dishes.

Overall, very happy with the purchase.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher a month ago, and it has been a major disappointment.
Comments (English): [ Much louder than advertised ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher a month ago, and it has been a major disappointment. It's supposed to be 44 dB but I measure it at 58 to 60 dB. It makes a grinding noise about every 1 to 2 seconds during the wash and rinse cycles that can be heard from the next room. The insulation under the door also keeps dropping down into view. During the first week, I contacted the installer to see if the noise problem was due to the insulation problem. When he came out, he simply stuffed the insulation back up in there (it still falls down) and told me the noise level is what I should expect. I then contacted KitchenAid about the issue, and they sent someone to check it out. First, he took the insulation that was falling down and stuffed it behind the floor face plate (not where it's supposed to go). Then he did diagnostics on the unit and found nothing wrong. He said the sound I am hearing is normal. He claimed that the 44 dB rating applies only to the motor itself. He thinks the sound I'm hearing is the water splashing against the walls of the steel tub. He suggested I try to reposition the dirty dishes to block the side walls. I told him that the dishwasher makes the same sound whether it's half-full or completely full. Then he said that the holes in the spray arms are much smaller now than they used to be, which causes less water to shoot out. That sounds like it contradicts his explanation. The sound I hear seems to be coming from the pump every time the water spurts into the spray arms. I now use the time-delay feature, so the dishwasher starts after we are in bed. I am debating on asking for an exchange to the 39 dB model. I am attaching a video so you can hear the noise level. Turn the volume up and then you can decide for yourself if you want to live with this noise level before you buy.The two good things about this model are the Pro-Dry fan feature, and the expanded capacity to hold dishes.

Finally the control panel died so we had to pull the trigger and put her to rest. We did some research and decided that it looked as if Bosch was going to be our best bet. It was delivered to our home. Easy to understands instructions. Nicely built with meticulous application of the sound-proofing insulation. Since using it for 1month we have absolutely no complaints. Positive features no heating element on bottom and dishes dry perfectly. Third drawer surprisingly useful (who'd a thunk). Filter in bottom easy to remove and clean. It runs nearly without a sound. The light that shines on the floor is a nice feature so you don't interrupt a cycle. I am looking forward to it holding up in longevity as is mentioned in independent reviews. Thanks Bosch for a great productLori ( happy home owner)

Sentence (English): We've had our Bosch dishwasher for a month.
Comments (English): [ Jim review ] || ---------------- || We've had our Bosch dishwasher for a month. We're impressed at how clean it gets our dishes, no matter how much baked on food there is. The one disappointment is that it dries the dishes only in the Speed 60 mode and even then, it does not get the dishes dry. One generally expects pools of water here and there where there are indentations to collect, but the dishes are more than 50% wet after this cycle. We also notice that the overall configuration of the dish trays do not allow as many dishes to be loaded as the Samsung we had previously. The only real difference is that we paid double the price for what we were told by the salesperson is, a dishwasher that will last more than 5 years. Overall, it's okay. To be fair, we deducted 2 stars, one for the drying component and one for tray capacity. Some might say, why not for the price. It's a perceived value thing. Paying more, doesn't always equate to greater value.

Sentence (English): Finally, I bought a dishwasher.
Comments (English): Finally, I bought a dishwasher. When it comes to home appliances, LG is the best. I finally escaped from dishwashing hell. When I told my friends that I bought a dishwasher and was liberated from dishwashing hell, they all congratulated me and even applauded me^^. Every time I talked to my friends after using the dishwasher, they said, “I became an LG dishwasher ambassador.” LG should give me this award. I’ve been waiting for this day so long^^. My husband and I used to fight every day because we kept putting off the dishes. Now, we don’t have to fight about the dishes. The dishwasher is a whole new world. I put the larvae in the dishwasher and add one all-in-one detergent (you don’t have to use a separate rinse aid), and my work is done. How leisurely^^. When I have a lot of dishes, if I stand for more than 30 minutes and wash them, my back hurts, my legs hurt, and I get tired. I think everyone feels the same way. Now, whenever I put dishes or pots in the dishwasher, I hum a tune. When the dishwashing is finished, the door opens automatically so you can clean up the dishes the next day. It's the ultimate in convenience. Oily frying pans and dishes are so fluffy and clean. Dirty dishes look like they were born again. They shine brightly. The dishes are perfectly dried. There are no stains. I didn't know hot air drying was this good. I'm really impressed. No matter how cleanly you wash the dishes, because of the remaining detergent, you end up drinking a few cups of Pong Pong in a year. LG dishwashers have 100C True Steam high-temperature sterilization and True Drying. They remove 99.99% of harmful bacteria and viruses, so you can be assured of the remaining detergent. Now you won't have to eat detergent^^. I feel healthier after using the dishwasher^^. The LG Dios dishwasher is a gift from God that frees you from the hard labor of washing dishes, saves time, cleans dishes, provides convenience, and even takes care of your health. The LG Dios dishwasher has a three-layer internal structure with washing wings in the middle and bottom, so it has excellent cleaning power. The advantages of the LG Dios dishwasher are that it can wash a large amount of dishes, starting with large pots, and the automatic door-opening function allows you to sleep soundly without worrying about it even if you turn on the dishwasher before going to bed. It also makes almost no noise. The cleaning power is also very good. The compartments for storing dishes are carefully separated, which is very convenient. The inverter also reduces electricity bills. Water usage is reduced when washing dishes. The biggest advantage is that you can be freed from the stress of washing dishes and the hell of dishwashing. Even if guests come and eat just one meal, the dishes pile up and it is a hell of dishwashing, but now, thanks to the LG dishwasher, even if you use a lot of dishes, you can have a cup of tea comfortably. I'm not dreaming, right? Thank you, LG Electronics, for giving me this comfort. Thank you again^^

Every time I talked to my friends after using the dishwasher, they said, “I became an LG dishwasher ambassador.” LG should give me this award. I’ve been waiting for this day so long^^. My husband and I used to fight every day because we kept putting off the dishes. Now, we don’t have to fight about the dishes. The dishwasher is a whole new world. I put the larvae in the dishwasher and add one all-in-one detergent (you don’t have to use a separate rinse aid), and my work is done. How leisurely^^. When I have a lot of dishes, if I stand for more than 30 minutes and wash them, my back hurts, my legs hurt, and I get tired. I think everyone feels the same way. Now, whenever I put dishes or pots in the dishwasher, I hum a tune. When the dishwashing is finished, the door opens automatically so you can clean up the dishes the next day. It's the ultimate in convenience. Oily frying pans and dishes are so fluffy and clean. Dirty dishes look like they were born again. They shine brightly. The dishes are perfectly dried. There are no stains. I didn't know hot air drying was this good. I'm really impressed. No matter how cleanly you wash the dishes, because of the remaining detergent, you end up drinking a few cups of Pong Pong in a year. LG dishwashers have 100C True Steam high-temperature sterilization and True Drying. They remove 99.99% of harmful bacteria and viruses, so you can be assured of the remaining detergent. Now you won't have to eat detergent^^. I feel healthier after using the dishwasher^^. The LG Dios dishwasher is a gift from God that frees you from the hard labor of washing dishes, saves time, cleans dishes, provides convenience, and even takes care of your health. The LG Dios dishwasher has a three-layer internal structure with washing wings in the middle and bottom, so it has excellent cleaning power. The advantages of the LG Dios dishwasher are that it can wash a large amount of dishes, starting with large pots, and the automatic door-opening function allows you to sleep soundly without worrying about it even if you turn on the dishwasher before going to bed. It also makes almost no noise. The cleaning power is also very good. The compartments for storing dishes are carefully separated, which is very convenient. The inverter also reduces electricity bills. Water usage is reduced when washing dishes. The biggest advantage is that you can be freed from the stress of washing dishes and the hell of dishwashing. Even if guests come and eat just one meal, the dishes pile up and it is a hell of dishwashing, but now, thanks to the LG dishwasher, even if you use a lot of dishes, you can have a cup of tea comfortably. I'm not dreaming, right? Thank you, LG Electronics, for giving me this comfort. Thank you again^^

Every time I talked to my friends after using the dishwasher, they said, “I became an LG dishwasher ambassador.” LG should give me this award. I’ve been waiting for this day so long^^. My husband and I used to fight every day because we kept putting off the dishes. Now, we don’t have to fight about the dishes. The dishwasher is a whole new world. I put the larvae in the dishwasher and add one all-in-one detergent (you don’t have to use a separate rinse aid), and my work is done. How leisurely^^. When I have a lot of dishes, if I stand for more than 30 minutes and wash them, my back hurts, my legs hurt, and I get tired. I think everyone feels the same way. Now, whenever I put dishes or pots in the dishwasher, I hum a tune. When the dishwashing is finished, the door opens automatically so you can clean up the dishes the next day. It's the ultimate in convenience. Oily frying pans and dishes are so fluffy and clean. Dirty dishes look like they were born again. They shine brightly. The dishes are perfectly dried. There are no stains. I didn't know hot air drying was this good. I'm really impressed. No matter how cleanly you wash the dishes, because of the remaining detergent, you end up drinking a few cups of Pong Pong in a year. LG dishwashers have 100C True Steam high-temperature sterilization and True Drying. They remove 99.99% of harmful bacteria and viruses, so you can be assured of the remaining detergent. Now you won't have to eat detergent^^. I feel healthier after using the dishwasher^^. The LG Dios dishwasher is a gift from God that frees you from the hard labor of washing dishes, saves time, cleans dishes, provides convenience, and even takes care of your health. The LG Dios dishwasher has a three-layer internal structure with washing wings in the middle and bottom, so it has excellent cleaning power. The advantages of the LG Dios dishwasher are that it can wash a large amount of dishes, starting with large pots, and the automatic door-opening function allows you to sleep soundly without worrying about it even if you turn on the dishwasher before going to bed. It also makes almost no noise. The cleaning power is also very good. The compartments for storing dishes are carefully separated, which is very convenient. The inverter also reduces electricity bills. Water usage is reduced when washing dishes. The biggest advantage is that you can be freed from the stress of washing dishes and the hell of dishwashing. Even if guests come and eat just one meal, the dishes pile up and it is a hell of dishwashing, but now, thanks to the LG dishwasher, even if you use a lot of dishes, you can have a cup of tea comfortably. I'm not dreaming, right? Thank you, LG Electronics, for giving me this comfort. Thank you again^^

It's doing a fantastic job.I would have liked a few "premium" features, like that wonderful third rack at the top for weird flat things and utensils, but at this price point I'm happy enough with it. The bottom rack is just wide open. I can dump anything in there, pots, pans, big serving plates, cutting boards, etc. They sell dishwashers claiming to be quieter, but I don't see the point. With the insulation wrap in place and properly boxed in it's already one of those "did it turn on? " kind of quiets when it runs. Cycle time is quite a bit longer than the one it replaced, but enh. whatever. I don't run even a load a day, so this isn't an issue. If you're really pounding dishes in a larger family a three-hour cycle might be a bit much, but I just turn it on and leave after dinner and unload in the morning.Getting "spotless dishes" is about more than just your washing machine. You also need good detergent, and good water. You can use a $1200 Boche and your dishes are still going to look like crap if you use a bottle of generic Dollar Store detergent. Hard water also makes soap work poorly; while they do make some "hard water" specialty detergents that include a bit of salt, check your PH. I had insanely hard water and my dishes looked terrible. I added a very small softener system that only softened water to the washing machine and the dishwasher (because I hate the feel of showering in softened water, it's gross. ) and the dishes improved by 80% with just that alone, even using the cheapest detergent you can buy. Upgrade that a few cents a load to premium packs and the glasses started coming out crystal clear, like they were new again. That was well worth the money and significantly improved the removal of stuck on food and making things "clean" even with an old used Craigslist dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Pros: 1) I love the 2 drawers.
Comments (English): [ Great features, needs some improvements ] || ---------------- || Pros: 1) I love the 2 drawers. 2) Running the washer every other day in a 2-person household lowers the water usage. 3) It's very quiet, I don't even know when it's running. 4) Love the ease to clean filters, et. al. 5) Rinse Aid plus using Ultra Dry really does dry well! Only the plastic lid edges remain wet. Cons: 1) Really need indicator lights for one and off (see Pro 3). 2) Need to lighten up the inside of the boxes because it's too dark (better yet, change the plastic to stainless steel, the heat radiating from steel would help dry). 3) The leftover water on the top rims. I have an excellent service center that has been adjusting the level of the washer and will come out again to adjust so the washer is tipped back just a hair to prevent the water from staying here. I have Rinse Aid and I'm adding in the Ultra Dry cycle but nothing removes that leftover water. I suspect it should not be there at all. After one of the adjustments, it stopped collecting on the left side but it's perfectly level now and still collecting in the front. See snapshot. Informative: 1) Converting to this from a standard dishwasher means re-learning where to put objects. 2) The manual lists the inner lid needing to seal. It warns that protruding objects might prevent sealing. It might be worth mentioning that an object can "protrude" if it's on the rack at an angle, so that only one edge is too high. Until I have more experience with my own items, I've been checking the placement carefully. Recommend that the dishwasher error if the lid can't seal. 3) Recommend the Ultra Dry option be available for the Normal wash cycle. I have to waste more water and lose my Energy Star water use because a Normal wash leaves dishes too wet. 4) GE could really permit the option to choose different color handles from the outset, rather than charging $400 (! ) for a pair of replacements. Black on black would look wonderful in my kitchen but not at that price. It's just gouging and really you shouldn't be proud of yourselves for such greed.

Sentence (English): As others have said, Bosch has managed to change dishwashers, a category that is normally a yawner, into something exciting.
Comments (English): [ The Hype is Justified (Bosch 800 vs 300 Compared) ] || ---------------- || As others have said, Bosch has managed to change dishwashers, a category that is normally a yawner, into something exciting. Once you've owned a Bosch, it's easy to see what the hype is about. In our case, we have experience with both this Bosch 800 series and a Bosch 300 series that's currently for sale (SHEM63W55N). For those on the fence, we wanted to share our opinions on both to help you decide. For those that need the short version, this can be summed up in one sentence: You can't go wrong with either, but if you are already spending nearly $1,000 for a 300 Series, the CrystalDry feature of the 800 Series makes the extra cost a good investment. Bosch 800 (SHPM78Z55N) vs. 300 (SHEM63W55N). Cleaning. Both models seem to clean identically, which is to say that they both do a FANTASTIC job. Items that our old dishwasher used to struggle with come out perfectly clean with Bosch. Even items on the top third rack come out looking spotless. We've stopped using the removable utensil rack on the bottom and just put utensils in the slots on the third rack, which frees up extra space on the bottom. Noise. We had the 300 in a different house with nicer cabinets and countertops than the 800, so it is not fair to do a direct comparison here. What we will say is that they are both very quiet, and whether they are even audible at all when running will depend on how nice your cabinets & countertops are, what items you are washing, and your proximity to the unit when it's on. The only sound we've ever heard from ours is the faint sound of the water jets spraying over large metal items like cookie sheets. Without those in the cycle, we don't hear anything. Buttons. This 800 series has touch-sensitive controls on the top, whereas the 300 (SHEM63W55N) has physical buttons on the front. The other 300 Series models with top controls also employ buttons in this location. Based on our experience, there is a trade-off in function vs. form here. The touch-sensitive controls on the 800 make the control surfaces feel more premium, but require a bit of finesse to use. By comparison, the physical buttons on the 300 are more straightforward to use, but don't feel quite as premium. That makes this comparison a subjective one, and your preferences may be different than ours. We could go either way on this one. Drying. This is really the only significant difference between the 300 and 800 Series during our use. The 300 Series uses condensation drying only, meaning it heats the dishes up with very hot water so that the water evaporates off of them. This works surprisingly well with glass and metal items, but plastic does not retain heat very well so the condensation drying is not as effective on these items. Large plastic items like Tupperware can sometimes require a lot of hand drying upon completion with the 300. By comparison, with the 800 and CrystalDry enabled, even the plastics come out almost totally dry. In our estimation, it provides the same performance you would get from a premium dishwasher with a traditional heating element. Conclusion. Both the 300 and 800 Series are both fantastic dishwashers, and you can't go wrong with either. If you use a ton of plastics or are very picky about how dry things are once cycles are finished, our opinion is that the $300ish extra to get the 800 is worth the investment.

Once you've owned a Bosch, it's easy to see what the hype is about. In our case, we have experience with both this Bosch 800 series and a Bosch 300 series that's currently for sale (SHEM63W55N). For those on the fence, we wanted to share our opinions on both to help you decide. For those that need the short version, this can be summed up in one sentence: You can't go wrong with either, but if you are already spending nearly $1,000 for a 300 Series, the CrystalDry feature of the 800 Series makes the extra cost a good investment. Bosch 800 (SHPM78Z55N) vs. 300 (SHEM63W55N). Cleaning. Both models seem to clean identically, which is to say that they both do a FANTASTIC job. Items that our old dishwasher used to struggle with come out perfectly clean with Bosch. Even items on the top third rack come out looking spotless. We've stopped using the removable utensil rack on the bottom and just put utensils in the slots on the third rack, which frees up extra space on the bottom. Noise. We had the 300 in a different house with nicer cabinets and countertops than the 800, so it is not fair to do a direct comparison here. What we will say is that they are both very quiet, and whether they are even audible at all when running will depend on how nice your cabinets & countertops are, what items you are washing, and your proximity to the unit when it's on. The only sound we've ever heard from ours is the faint sound of the water jets spraying over large metal items like cookie sheets. Without those in the cycle, we don't hear anything. Buttons. This 800 series has touch-sensitive controls on the top, whereas the 300 (SHEM63W55N) has physical buttons on the front. The other 300 Series models with top controls also employ buttons in this location. Based on our experience, there is a trade-off in function vs. form here. The touch-sensitive controls on the 800 make the control surfaces feel more premium, but require a bit of finesse to use. By comparison, the physical buttons on the 300 are more straightforward to use, but don't feel quite as premium. That makes this comparison a subjective one, and your preferences may be different than ours. We could go either way on this one. Drying. This is really the only significant difference between the 300 and 800 Series during our use. The 300 Series uses condensation drying only, meaning it heats the dishes up with very hot water so that the water evaporates off of them. This works surprisingly well with glass and metal items, but plastic does not retain heat very well so the condensation drying is not as effective on these items. Large plastic items like Tupperware can sometimes require a lot of hand drying upon completion with the 300. By comparison, with the 800 and CrystalDry enabled, even the plastics come out almost totally dry. In our estimation, it provides the same performance you would get from a premium dishwasher with a traditional heating element. Conclusion. Both the 300 and 800 Series are both fantastic dishwashers, and you can't go wrong with either. If you use a ton of plastics or are very picky about how dry things are once cycles are finished, our opinion is that the $300ish extra to get the 800 is worth the investment.

I have been very disappointed with this dishwasher.

Comments (English): [ it's the best ] || ---------------- || This is a dishwasher that I ordered after thinking about it for several years. It was difficult to install because it was not standard. On the day of reservation, the lg engineer came and made another reservation for another day because the furniture was renovated. There was a lot of wood dust during the renovation, but since they worked in the hallway of the apartment, there was only minimal dust and a lot of noise in the house, but I felt less sorry for the neighbors because it was a weekday morning. .) In the afternoon, an lg engineer came and installed the machine, and he worked for about 2 hours and 20 minutes before leaving. Each house structure has a level of difficulty, but it seems that my house was not an easy structure. Now, since it was installed on the opposite side of the drain in the kitchen, it was essential to extend the water supply and drain hose. There was no electrical outlet nearby, so he made a small hole in the marble top of the sink and added an extension multi-tap. When fixing the machine, keep checking to keep it level. Connecting the water supply hose also causes scars because the space is narrow. The driver wrote a lot. Thanks to that, it was installed very nicely. When I put it on, it works very well. It cleans all heavy dishes, pots, and frying pans, so I feel freed from dishwashing hell. It's comfortable to use even if you use multiple cups and turn it around. I like the product even more because it's a new product produced this year. Those who are worried, live quickly! ^^ (Details of additional cost. Furniture remodeling cost: KRW 180,000 Electricity multi-tap addition: KRW 38,000 This part seems to vary depending on the installation situation.)

Sentence (English): As others have said, Bosch has managed to change dishwashers, a category that is normally a yawner, into something exciting.
Comments (English): [ The Hype is Justified (Bosch 800 vs 300 Compared) ] || ---------------- || As others have said, Bosch has managed to change dishwashers, a category that is normally a yawner, into something exciting. Once you've owned a Bosch, it's easy to see what the hype is about.In our case, we have experience with both this Bosch 800 series and a Bosch 300 series that's currently for sale (SHEM63W55N). For those on the fence, we wanted to share our opinions on both to help you decide.For those that need the short version, this can be summed up in one sentence: You can't go wrong with either, but if you are already spending nearly $1,000 for a 300 Series, the CrystalDry feature of the 800 Series makes the extra cost a good investment. Bosch 800 (SHPM78Z55N) vs. 300 (SHEM63W55N)CleaningBoth models seem to clean identically, which is to say that they both do a FANTASTIC job. Items that our old dishwasher used to struggle with come out perfectly clean with Bosch. Even items on the top third rack come out looking spotless. We've stopped using the removable utensil rack on the bottom and just put utensils in the slots on the third rack, which frees up extra space on the bottom.NoiseWe had the 300 in a different house with nicer cabinets and countertops than the 800, so it is not fair to do a direct comparison here. What we will say is that they are both very quiet, and whether they are even audible at all when running will depend on how nice your cabinets & countertops are, what items you are washing, and your proximity to the unit when it's on. The only sound we've ever heard from ours is the faint sound of the water jets spraying over large metal items like cookie sheets. Without those in the cycle, we don't hear anything. ButtonsThis 800 series has touch-sensitive controls on the top, whereas the 300 (SHEM63W55N) has physical buttons on the front. The other 300 Series models with top controls also employ buttons in this location. Based on our experience, there is a trade-off in function vs. form here. The touch-sensitive controls on the 800 make the control surfaces feel more premium, but require a bit of finesse to use. By comparison, the physical buttons on the 300 are more straightforward to use, but don't feel quite as premium. That makes this comparison a subjective one, and your preferences may be different than ours. We could go either way on this one.DryingThis is really the only significant difference between the 300 and 800 Series during our use. The 300 Series uses condensation drying only, meaning it heats the dishes up with very hot water so that the water evaporates off of them. This works surprisingly well with glass and metal items, but plastic does not retain heat very well so the condensation drying is not as effective on these items. Large plastic items like Tupperware can sometimes require a lot of hand drying upon completion with the 300. By comparison, with the 800 and CrystalDry enabled, even the plastics come out almost totally dry. In our estimation, it provides the same performance you would get from a premium dishwasher with a traditional heating element. ConclusionBoth the 300 and 800 Series are both fantastic dishwashers, and you can't go wrong with either. If you use a ton of plastics or are very picky about how dry things are once cycles are finished, our opinion is that the $300ish extra to get the 800 is worth the investment.

For those on the fence, we wanted to share our opinions on both to help you decide.For those that need the short version, this can be summed up in one sentence: You can't go wrong with either, but if you are already spending nearly $1,000 for a 300 Series, the CrystalDry feature of the 800 Series makes the extra cost a good investment. Bosch 800 (SHPM78Z55N) vs. 300 (SHEM63W55N)CleaningBoth models seem to clean identically, which is to say that they both do a FANTASTIC job. Items that our old dishwasher used to struggle with come out perfectly clean with Bosch. Even items on the top third rack come out looking spotless. We've stopped using the removable utensil rack on the bottom and just put utensils in the slots on the third rack, which frees up extra space on the bottom.NoiseWe had the 300 in a different house with nicer cabinets and countertops than the 800, so it is not fair to do a direct comparison here. What we will say is that they are both very quiet, and whether they are even audible at all when running will depend on how nice your cabinets & countertops are, what items you are washing, and your proximity to the unit when it's on. The only sound we've ever heard from ours is the faint sound of the water jets spraying over large metal items like cookie sheets. Without those in the cycle, we don't hear anything. ButtonsThis 800 series has touch-sensitive controls on the top, whereas the 300 (SHEM63W55N) has physical buttons on the front. The other 300 Series models with top controls also employ buttons in this location. Based on our experience, there is a trade-off in function vs. form here. The touch-sensitive controls on the 800 make the control surfaces feel more premium, but require a bit of finesse to use. By comparison, the physical buttons on the 300 are more straightforward to use, but don't feel quite as premium. That makes this comparison a subjective one, and your preferences may be different than ours. We could go either way on this one.DryingThis is really the only significant difference between the 300 and 800 Series during our use. The 300 Series uses condensation drying only, meaning it heats the dishes up with very hot water so that the water evaporates off of them. This works surprisingly well with glass and metal items, but plastic does not retain heat very well so the condensation drying is not as effective on these items. Large plastic items like Tupperware can sometimes require a lot of hand drying upon completion with the 300. By comparison, with the 800 and CrystalDry enabled, even the plastics come out almost totally dry. In our estimation, it provides the same performance you would get from a premium dishwasher with a traditional heating element. ConclusionBoth the 300 and 800 Series are both fantastic dishwashers, and you can't go wrong with either. If you use a ton of plastics or are very picky about how dry things are once cycles are finished, our opinion is that the $300ish extra to get the 800 is worth the investment.

Sentence (English): I bought this model about 4 1/2 years ago, the bottle jets, adjustable 2nd rack and 3rd rack were a selling points for me.
Comments (English): [ Didn't last, wasn't great at its job either ] || ---------------- || I bought this model about 4 1/2 years ago, the bottle jets, adjustable 2nd rack and 3rd rack were a selling points for me. It flooded my kitchen a couple nights ago, and rained down into the basement below as well. A plumber came and said the pump broke and that replacing it would cost as much as a new one. Obviously not happy about having to replace this after only 5 years! I'm now spending far too much time researching replacement dishwashers: features, brands, user reviews and availability. When a home appliance unexpectedly dies in a family of 7, time is of the essence. Living on disposable dishes and forcing people to eat sandwiches for too long will lead to a revolt. As for its performance before complete & premature failure. Older dishwashers did a much better job at washing & especially drying. The eco friendly models that are being sold now are a wonderful idea, but leave a lot to be desired in performance and this goes for most brands in the past 20 years. This model didn't dry much at all, eventually I just shut off the drying feature, opened the door after a cycle, dumped the little pools of water off certain items and let them air dry. The washing cycles were painfully long, like ridiculous. God forbid you didn't run it the night before because it took nearly 3 hours to complete a normal cycle. Dishes came out ok, most of the time. Anything semi-dried on was definitely not coming off though and with such a long cycle, dirty dishes piled up waiting for their turn. I always rinse the food off, but rinsing things spotless before putting them in the dishwasher seems to make the major purpose of a dishwasher obsolete. Plenty of times, we would have to run it a 2nd (painfully long) time because grime would somehow just be distributed throughout the washer. The adjustable tine rows on the bottom rack never quite locked into place, making plates rattle around more. The silverware basket plastic on the bottom started breaking off after 3 years, letting utensils slide down into the tub, unnoticed until too late, interfering with the sprayer and thus the cleaning. I had to purchase a replacement basket for $40 last year. Also, the basket comes in 3 separate pieces which “lock” together. It is annoying if you are the type that likes to pull out the silverware basket to unload because it never came out as a single, locked together, piece. A cosmetic plastic strip around the top of the door started peeling off recently and required some superglue assistance. One last mentionable thing, which is partially on me for not measuring before I purchased, is that our plates are square and a guess a little bigger than the average plate, unless the 2nd row was all the way up, the sprayer hit them. Also true for any taller than average utensils in the basket-like my basic bread knives that seem normal size, but in the wrong spot, we're smacked by the sprayer and when the sprayer doesn't have free reign, the 3 hour cycle is ruined. I understand that if you hear something bumping, you need to go back in & fix it, but since the wash cycle took so long, we usually ran it just before bedtime and were not near it when the sprayer began moving. Pros: it was quiet, bottle sprayers are a nice concept and seemed work, easy adjustable height on 2nd rack is essential.

Comments (English): [ Great concept, poorly executed. ] || ---------------- || We have had this dishwasher for 8 months and I wish I would have returned it when the first piece broke 2 months in. I love the idea of a third tray for small things but the height taken up with the third tray drastically limits what we are able to put in it. The reason I gave it a two-star rating is because it did a decent job of cleaning dishes for a few weeks. However, the movable parts on the inside, such as the fold down prongs, are held on by cheap clips that keep breaking and now don't stay up, so the dishes keep falling everywhere. Also, the top handle is a very thin piece of plastic and directly on the top of the thin plastic handle is the power button that needs to be pressed pretty hard to start so the plastic handle broke from the pressure. We have been happy with Samsung products in the past but feel that they cut too many corners on this model. Not looking forward to spending another 1,000 on a dishwasher so soon.

This machine stopped working after 15 days. One day the machine had code \"888\" flashing on its display panel and no longer worked. I googled this code - and found it could be something liked a failed pump and could not see anything obvious in the unit itself ( ex: food jammed in the filter or something). When I called the Best Buy TOTAL TECH warrant center to get assistance/ request a service tech, the person had no guidance for any suggestions for the \"888\" code could be. The Best Buy TOTAL TECH person then indicated they would send a repair tech within 3 WEEKS so they could look at/repair my 15 day old dishwasher. Was disappointed about the long lead time to say the least. :-(. This week the Best Buy Tech did come out for the scheduled service call. It turned out food had been stuck under the removable filter basket (which I could not see). Once this was removed and he flushed out the draining hose, the dishwasher was working again. Really hoping this machine will not turn into a maintenance headache. If you are going to buy this machine , I suggest you get the TOTAL TECH extended membership just in case.
